name: blowdown-seat
title: Blowdown Seat
description: A rate-limiter shed-threshold configurator drawn as a spring safety-valve cutaway: the disc lifts off its seat the instant live load crosses the upper `pop` threshold and refuses to reseat until load falls all the way below a separate, lower `reseat` mark — real two-threshold hysteresis, set with two mutually-clamped range-slider handles that can never be dragged or keyed closer than 3 percentage points apart.
useWhen: a shed/vent-style rate-limiter or circuit-breaker control where the operator sets two related thresholds — a shed-start point and a lower shed-stop point — and the two handles must be mechanically prevented from collapsing into one number. Pick meter-threshold-trip instead for a read-only alert with no user-adjustable thresholds (`value` is its only input); pick slider-range-shear instead for an ordinary min/max range filter with no lifted/latched state and no minimum-gap constraint between the handles.
instruction: Renders one governing scalar, P = liveRate / capacity as a percentage, against two operator-set thresholds on a shared vertical pressure ruler: `pop` (shed-start, drawn above) and `reseat` (shed-stop, drawn below), each a real `<input type="range">` (role=slider for free) rather than a custom draggable div. The disc stays seated on the valve while P is below `pop`, lifts the instant P crosses `pop`, and — the whole point of the component — does NOT reseat the moment P dips back under `pop`; it only reseats once P falls below the separate, lower `reseat` mark. This is genuine two-threshold hysteresis: a `lifted` boolean is flipped only by an edge-triggered effect watching `liveRate` cross `popEff` upward or `reseatEff` downward (mirroring this registry's meter-threshold-trip latch/re-arm effect), never by a continuous comparison, so any P sitting between `reseat` and `pop` reads as whatever `lifted` was already pinned to. Unlike meter-threshold-trip's binary latch, the 'latch' here is a continuously-varying physical lift: while lifted, lift height (`liftFrac`, capped so it's never literally 0 or a full detach) tracks how far P currently sits above `reseat`, so the valve reads as one physical mechanism responding continuously, not a meter driving a separate discrete counter. The gap between the two thresholds is mechanically floored at 3 percentage points (`MIN_GAP`), enforced two ways at once: each handle's own `min`/`max` attribute is pinned live to the OTHER handle's current committed value +/-3, so keyboard stepping (arrow keys, Home/End, Page Up/Down — free from using a native range input) can never build a sub-3 gap, and a drawn 'blowdown ring' between the two handles on the ruler visibly compresses toward, but never past, that same floor as `reseat` is dragged up toward `pop`. Pointer interaction is a single invisible hit-rect spanning the ruler; on pointerdown it picks whichever handle's current y-position is nearer the click (the same proximity-arbitration technique as this registry's slider-range-shear), focuses that handle's real input, and clamps every subsequent drag position to the mutual floor — there is no way to reach a single-threshold configuration from either pointer or keyboard. Vent flow and a running shed counter (both a per-cycle count and a running total) are derived purely from `liftFrac` and the excess of `liveRate` over the reseat-rate floor — no separate state to keep in sync with the lift — and accumulate only across the interval the valve was actually lifted, using a delta-time effect capped at 0.5s per tick so a paused tab can't produce one giant spurious shed spike on resume. A polite `aria-live` region announces only the two edge crossings ('vent open' / 'vent closed', the latter including the shed count for that cycle) — never a per-frame update — so it stays legible even under a noisy signal that wobbles around a threshold. The disc's lift and the drawn spring's compression both transition on distinct curves depending on what triggered the change: a stiff overshooting back-out curve (260ms) on the lift-off crossing, a slower no-overshoot ease (520ms) on the reseat crossing, and a quick untensioned ease (180ms) for ordinary in-band tracking — all collapsed to 0ms under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` (checked live via a `matchMedia` change listener), while the vent-flow glyph animation is separately killed by a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` CSS override. The entire valve cutaway — body, bonnet, seat rim, spring zigzag, disc, vent nozzle, ruler, blowdown ring, live-pressure marker — is `aria-hidden`; the two range inputs, the live region, and a plain-language status paragraph (`aria-describedby` on both inputs) stating the current seated/venting state and both thresholds in rps carry the entire accessible surface. DOM+SVG+CSS only, no canvas — every stroke and fill is a `stroke-current`/`fill-current` token utility class (`text-border`, `text-ns-muted`, `text-foreground`, `text-ns-accent` only on the focus ring), never a hex literal, so both themes restyle for free.
